donor_statement: CONFIRMED UPSTREAM. HEST issue #133 (closed, 2026-03-22): the maintainer (pauldoucet, COLLABORATOR) states 'the patient information for this cohort was wrong in HEST v1.1.0 (as reported in issue #126) and was corrected in HEST v1.3.0', and that they 'chose not to update HEST-bench COAD splits as we're still satisfying the core requirement of ensuring the same patient does not appear in both the train and test splits for any given fold'. The issue body gives the v1.3.0 mapping: TENX147 -> patient 5, TENX148 -> patient 2, TENX149 -> patient 1.
notes: 10x aggregator page for "Characterization of immune cell populations in the tumor microenvironment of colorectal cancer using high definition spatial profiling" (Oliveira et al., Nat Genet 2025, GSE280318) lists three separate Xenium resourceIds — Xenium_V1_Human_Colon_Cancer_P1_CRC_Add_on_FFPE, _P2_CRC_, _P5_CRC_ — each tied to a distinct patient (Table 1 of the paper: P1CRC/P2CRC/P5CRC are three of five different CRC donors). This positively contradicts the r5b_sample_inventory label of "Patient 1" for all three of TENX147/148/149, which is HEST v1.1.0-era metadata. HEST maintainer (GitHub issue #133, pauldoucet) confirmed the v1.1.0 patient info for this cohort was wrong and was corrected in v1.3.0 to TENX147->patient5, TENX148->patient2, TENX149->patient1 (three distinct patients) — but this specific TENX-id-to-P# correspondence is HEST-internal (reported secondhand on GitHub, not independently re-derivable from 10x's page, which does not expose HEST sample IDs). donor_id below follows that HEST-corrected mapping for traceability, flagged as not independently cross-checked beyond "these are three distinct donors."

correction: UPGRADED by lead from 'HEST-mapping, uncorroborated' to corroborated: the v1.3.0 patient mapping is quoted in the issue body and confirmed by the maintainer's reply, both read directly from the GitHub API rather than taken from the audit's summary. Consequence for this project, which the issue does not draw: because the bench splits were deliberately left as-is, COAD fold 0 holds out TENX147+148+149 together - three donors at once - and trains on TENX111 alone, while fold 1 holds out TENX111 and trains on three donors. The maintainer's stated requirement is met, but COAD's patient gap is a 3-donor holdout trained on a single donor, which is why it is the largest of any task and why it is not comparable with the other tasks' 1-donor holdouts.

Both named 10x product pages were checked directly: page 1 (ffpe-human-pancreas-with-xenium-multimodal-cell-segmentation-1-standard) has donorCount:"1", single resourceId (Xenium_V1_human_Pancreas_FFPE), tissue "purchased from AcePix Biosciences" (Stage III Adenocarcinoma). donor_statement: Janesick et al. 2023 Nat Commun (DOI 10.1038/s41467-023-43458-x) GEO deposit GSE243280 (SuperSeries of GSE243168 [Xenium] + GSE243275 [scRNA-seq/Visium]) is the cited primary source ("two samples published in [Janesick2023]" per HEST paper text for NCBI783/NCBI785). GSE243280 contains exactly 4 spatial (image-bearing) GSMs total: GSM7780153/7780154 = Xenium Rep1/Rep2 of Sample #1 (= TENX95/TENX99, one donor, per the Series_overall_design text), GSM7780155 = the single Xenium section of Sample #2 (Discovery Life Sciences 2nd FFPE block, pT2 pN1a pMX ER-/HER2+/PR- -- a genuinely DIFFERENT donor from Sample #1), and GSM7782699 = the single Visium CytAssist GSM ("Two replicate 5um sections were taken... for Visium CytAssist" -- both replicates from Sample #1, i.e. same donor as TENX95/TENX99). HEST's own metadata table (which would state the exact GSM<->"NCBI78x" correspondence) is gated on Hugging Face (401) and the redistribution mirror (hest-bench) file-transfer CDN (us.aws.cdn.hf.co) is outside the network allowlist, so the specific NCBI783<->GSM and NCBI785<->GSM mapping could NOT be independently confirmed. What IS established: there are only 2 true donors (Sample #1, Sample #2) among the 4 spatial GSMs in this deposit, yet HEST assigns 4 different "patient" numbers (patient 5, patient 4, plus TENX95="patient 2", TENX99="patient 1") to all 4 IDC-task samples. If NCBI783/785 map onto the Visium GSM (Sample #1) and the Sample #2 Xenium GSM respectively (the only two non-duplicate spatial datasets left after TENX95/99 already claim Rep1/Rep2), then one of NCBI783/NCBI785 shares a donor with TENX95/TENX99, and the IDC task's 4 "different-patient" labels would reduce to just 2 real donors -- a larger version of the already-known fault. This is a plausible, source-motivated HYPOTHESIS, not a confirmed mapping, and is reported as such: exact identity of NCBI783 and NCBI785 individually is unverifiable without the gated file.

notes: GSM GSM5732360 !Sample_characteristics_ch1 = "donor: Patient_8". Source: Liu et al. 2022 Nat Commun (DOI 10.1038/s41467-022-34581-2), spatial-transcriptomics GEO deposit GSE190811 ("...breast cancer patients (10x Visium)"), which contains exactly 4 GSMs, matching HEST's 4 LYMPH_IDC samples. notes: Source: Meylan et al. 2022 Immunity (DOI 10.1016/j.immuni.2022.02.001), spatial-transcriptomics GEO deposit GSE175540 ("Spatial transcriptomics of fresh frozen ccRCC human tumors"). Contains exactly 24 GSMs (GSM5924030-GSM5924053), matching HEST's 24 INT samples. GSM titles are 24 DISTINCT tumor identifiers drawn from three named cohorts: "ffpe_c_{2,3,4,7,10,20,21,34,36,39,45,51}" (12 samples), "frozen_a_{1,3,15,17}" (4), "frozen_b_{1,7,13,18}" (4), "frozen_c_{2,5,23,57}" (4) -- matching a secondary source's description of "Tumor samples from three ccRCC cohorts... 24 tumors...characterized by Visium". All 24 titles are unique, positively confirming 24 distinct tumor/patient samples, consistent with HEST's "Patient 1" through "Patient 24" distinct labels. Exact INT-id <-> specific GSM/cohort-number correspondence was not individually re-derived (HEST's gated metadata table would be needed for that), but the audit question at stake -- are all 24 samples genuinely different patients, with none merged or split -- is verified at the source level: 24 GSMs, 24 distinct titles, no duplicates.

donor_statement: Methods, Biomaterials: 'Human breast FFPE-preserved blocks were obtained from Avaden, BioIVT, and Discovery Life Sciences. The sample set comprised 11 blocks representing a range of breast cancer stages and grades, including both DCIS and invasive lesions, as well as one normal breast tissue sample (see Supplemental Table S1).' Results: variance 'was calculated across tumor cells from all 11 breast cancer sections (excluding normal - #S2-Top)'. Supplemental Table S1 gives one disease, stage, grade and hormone status per section; S1-Top is IDC, T3 N0 M0, G3, HER2-Neg. Twelve sections, twelve distinct clinical profiles, eleven cancer blocks plus one normal.
notes: HEST calls this section 'Section 1, top' and labels it 'Patient 1', grouping the three sections of each Section number under one patient. The source does not support that grouping: it states eleven cancer blocks for the eleven cancer sections, and Supplemental Table S1 gives each section its own stage, grade and hormone status. The natural reading is that S1 to S4 are the four Xenium slides and top/middle/bottom are the three tissue pieces on each slide, so this set contributes eleven donors, not four. The source states blocks rather than donors, so the one-donor-per-block step is not positively stated; it is the reading the clinical table supports. HEST also assigns oncotree IDC to all eleven, which Table S1 contradicts for eight of them. The twelfth section, S2-Top (normal breast), is not in HEST; the TENX194 id is absent from every release table.

donor_statement: The study states 'we used non-infected, PFA-fixed lung and kidney organoids embedded in optimal cutting temperature embedding medium (OCT)', that 'between 6 and 8 organoids (<1 mm in diameter) were embedded together to fit within a single capture area (<42.25 mm2)', and that '3 tissue sections' were collected from the tissue block containing kidney organoids.
notes: Answered: this is fixed organoid material, not patient tissue. HEST's subseries 'PFA fixed kidney_organoid_3' is literal. The three HEST samples NCBI538, NCBI539 and NCBI540 are the three consecutive sections of one organoid block, so they are three sections of the same material rather than three independent units, and each section carries 6 to 8 separate organoids. HEST's disease_state 'Treated' and organ 'Kidney' are misleading for any analysis that treats these as kidney tissue. HEST's pixel_size_um_embedded is missing for all three, which is why resolution_uncertain is set.
